title: Geo routing chaos test plan and operator notes
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a working plan for running controlled chaos experiments against our region pinning and geo-routing enforcement logic for private deployments. Goal is to validate that enforcement policies (pinning, preferred-region routing, fallbacks) behave correctly under degraded conditions and that operator runbooks are sufficient for quick recovery. Also capture unexpected behaviors and telemetry gaps.

Scope (what we'll test):
- Enforcement toggles: strict pin, soft-preference, and no-pin fallback paths.
- Routing layer failures: control-plane delays, routing table corruptions, and region-to-region network partitions.
- Downstream capacity constraints: destination region full (no GPU capacity) and queueing/backpressure responses.
- Cache coherence: KV cache invalidation during fallback and cross-region cache re-writes.
- Telemetry: validate that decision reasons (pin, capacity, latency) are emitted and logged for sampling.

Out-of-scope for this run:
- KMS/HSM access failures (covered by security incident drills).
- Long-term residency policy changes (policy authoring will be separate).

Hypotheses to validate:
1) Strict-pinned customer requests never leave pinned region unless explicit emergency override is applied.
2) Under soft-preference, requests route to preferred region when healthy; when preferred is saturated, fallback path chooses lowest-latency compatible region.
3) Operator-initiated emergency-unpin trigger works and is visible in audit logs and console.
4) Telemetry contains: routing_reason, chosen_region, latency_ms, capacity_tags, and fallback_trigger_id. If any are missing, debugging time spikes.

Test scenarios (ordered by safety/risk):
A. Dry-run: inject 1% of traffic with header X-RW-CHAOS=geo-test to simulate routing decision but do not actually change route; record decisions.
B. Canary failover: for one non-prod customer, mark preferred region unhealthy in the control plane; observe routing and client responses.
C. Capacity saturation: simulate full capacity in EU-west by toggling available_gpus=0 in staging scheduler for 30s; watch backlog behavior and errors returned.
D. Network partition: delay/blackhole inter-region traffic between us-east and eu-west for 60s; assert strict-pin requests from EU continue to egress EU only; soft-pref requests should either queue or prefer other EU zones.
E. Routing table corruption (read-only): return malformed routing table entry for a small set of keys and measure fallback correctness and errors returned to callers.
F. Rollback / operator override: simulate emergency-unpin for an impacted SST and verify it is auditable and reversible.

Execution playbook (step-by-step):
1) Pre-run checklist (Ops + SRE + Eng on call present)
   - Announce window in #eng-private-deployments and #sre-alerts (24h and 1h reminders).
   - Take snapshot of routing config and policy flags (config-snap-<timestamp>).
   - Ensure on-call pager and escalation matrix is reachable.
   - Reserve a rollback slot and confirm DB backup for policy store.
2) Dry-run A -> run for 20 minutes, gather samples, review logs.
3) If dry-run clean, progress to Canary B on one staging customer for 10 minutes. Monitor key metrics.
4) If Canary stable, run C and D sequentially while keeping blast radius limited (5% traffic and a single customer set).
5) After each experiment, run the recovery checklist and wait a cool-down period (10 minutes or until metrics stable).

Safety controls / blast radius limits:
- Start with header-based simulation (no route change) before any real routing manipulation.
- Max traffic affected: 5% initially, can increase only after post-checks.
- Single-customer or single-account canary for disruptive tests.
- Auto-abort on: error-rate spike > 2x baseline for 5 consecutive minutes OR tail latency p95 > 2x baseline OR any strict-pin leakage detected.

Observability & telemetry to capture (required):
- routing_decision.reason (pin|preference|capacity|latency|fallback)
- routing_decision.chosen_region
- routing_decision.previous_region (if fallback)
- request.latency_ms
- scheduler.available_gpus
- policy.version
- audit.unpin_trigger_id
- sample stack traces for any 5xx errors within test window

Success criteria (pass/fail):
- PASS: No strict-pinned customer requests observed outside their pinned region (0 leaks in sampled logs).
- PASS: Soft-preference fallbacks choose region with compatible model and accept traffic without >5% elevated error rate.
- FAIL: Any unlogged emergency-unpin or manual route change outside documented operator flow.

Operator runbook snippets (quick reference):
- Detecting leakage:
  - Query: SELECT count(*) FROM routing_logs WHERE customer_id = <X> AND chosen_region != pinned_region AND timestamp >= <t>
  - If count > 0 open INC ticket and run emergency-unpin only after confirming audit trail.
- Emergency unpin (manual override, limited use):
  - Command (control plane API): POST /admin/policy/override { customer_id: X, override: "unpin-temp", expires_at: <iso> }
  - Create audit note in policy store UI and add link to ticket.
- Reconciliation after rollback:
  - Re-apply saved config-snap and validate routing_decision.version matches snapshot.

Post-test artifacts to produce:
- Test run spreadsheet with per-scenario metrics (p50/p95/p99 latencies, error rates, routing_reason distribution).
- Short incident playbook if any aborts happened with timeline.
- Gap analysis listing missing telemetry or unclear decision traces.

Dry-run checklist (detailed):
- [ ] Confirm telemetry retention window covers test (7d).
- [ ] Enable higher-sampling for routing logs for test TTL (increase from 1% to 25%).
- [ ] Ensure test keys use X-RW-ENV=staging and are marked in billing as test to avoid charge confusion.
- [ ] Prepare metric dashboards: per-region throughput, per-customer error rate, routing_reason heatmap.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Do we have a deterministic mapping of model-compatibility across regions? If not, we need a quick compatibility matrix for the test (models that can be served from EU vs US).
- How will Dedicated customers with multi-region pinning behave? Need separate test cases.
- Audit log sampling can hide rare leaks — consider temporarily increasing sample rate for strict-pinned customers during test.

Postmortem template (short):
- Summary: one-line result of the run.
- Timeline: minute-level events for aborts and rollbacks.
- Root cause: if any failure, attach traces and config versions.
- Actions: who will patch telemetry, who will add tests to CI, and when.

Next steps / assignments (rough):
- Priya: add a model-compatibility matrix and mark models that are region-locked (due EOD 2025-02-14).
- Liam: wiring up increased routing log sampling and a short dashboard (EOD 2025-02-12).
- Marco: prepare the staging scheduler toggle and capacity simulator (2025-02-17).
- Maya: coordinate run window, update this doc with final exec times, and own the postmortem.

Misc notes (informal):
- Keep run small and communicative. Operators hate surprises — include SRE and on-call infra in the run page.
- Expect small unhelpful errors (503s) during capacity saturation; focus on correctness of routing decisions over small transient errors.
- TODO: add the exact API payload examples and rollback curl commands in a follow-up doc.

End of doc.
